title: B16 original-checkpoint recovery progress and conditional latency witnesses
outcome: B16 original-checkpoint recovery progress and conditional latency witnesses
acceptance: Actual automatic tick scheduling leads to exact original checkpoint recovery success and actual SQLite Accepted/Confirmed settlement with released original exclusion under a clearly stated healthy-authority/no-owner-drift condition, recording scripted elapsed trigger-to-settlement.

Busy or transport-failed recovery uses a bounded fast retry series followed by a documented slower cadence through the existing shared retry scheduler, with bounded per-tick work and concurrency, fair service of other eligible operations, and restart behavior that does not renew the fast allowance. Read-only probe failures do not consume send attempts; durable send-boundary uncertainty is preserved. Accepted results can finish local accounting without another network send or exhaustion of the network-send allowance. Scripted tests cover exhaustion of the fast series, a later successful automatic orphan retry, restart during cooldown, concurrent triggers, probe failures and explicit capacity backpressure. No recovery path sends extra Bind/Evaluate/Begin or provider prompts, clears unrelated duties, or fabricates completion. Report the concrete cadence and conditional progress bound; no unconditional two-minute completion is claimed.

An independent healthy root remains dispatchable while the first root's Unknown recovery is held. Original-checkpoint recovery itself sends no SessionBind, Evaluate or Begin and no new provider prompt; while the original obligation remains unsettled, those mediated admission operations remain excluded. After exact original durable Accepted/Confirmed settlement, completed local ACK and release of only its matching original exclusion, a separately requested next turn may use the existing transport-rebind reconciliation path before Evaluate and Begin. Under healthy authority, successful current-owner reconciliation and no independent blocking duty, that turn delivers exactly one new provider prompt. Failed reconciliation, owner drift or an independent unresolved duty still prevents dispatch; settlement neither clears the generic rebind flag nor authorizes clearing unrelated duties.
